(Screen capture) Shorewood has completed an operational analysis of the Shorewood Community & Event Center (SCEC), providing a roadmap for future discussions about the facility's operations, programming, staffing and long-term sustainability. The City Council received the analysis information Sept. 14 and plans to discuss next steps further. "I think ISG and their team did a really great job. We had a very skilled task force group that come from a lot of different perspectives. There were people that have never set foot in that facility before, and there were people that are there every day of the week," Shorewood Parks and Recreation Director Mitchell Czech shared. The task force's key takeaways include: community value remains the foundation of future decision‑making, increased usage represents the greatest opportunity, marketing, awareness, and defining a clear market position are critical, future success will require strategic partnerships, programming and rental strategies should reflect community needs and market demand, and finally, financial sustainability should focus on cost recovery rather than full self‑sufficiency. Located at 5735 Country Club Road, the Shorewood Community & Event Center serves as a rental venue for private events, meetings and other gatherings, as well as a home for senior programming. With South Shore Senior Partners planning to disband by the end of 2026, the Shorewood City Council commissioned an operational analysis to examine the center’s current use, programming, staffing and finances and identify opportunities for its future. Earlier this year, the City Council established the community task force to work alongside staff and a consultant to evaluate how the facility is being used and identify opportunities for improvement. The study examined the Center's operations, utilization, programming, financial performance and long-term potential. The study was intended to help guide future decision-making as the City continues exploring ways to maximize community benefit, enhance programming and facility use, and ensure the Shorewood Community & Event Center remains a valuable community asset for years to come. Jay Lotthammer from ISG presented three options for the city council to consider, including: Stabilizing the facility with minimal new investment, accepting service reductions and limited operational improvement Maintaining today's service model through a modest staffing investment that replaces key SSSP functions Growing and activating the facility through additional staffing, programming, marketing, customer service and rental development "One effort should lead to another or you'll see it as good money after bad and then each scenario is interchangeable," Lotthammer said. "There's components of one that can move to the other." The first scenario would bring in a total of $89,000 in revenue and $155,371 in expenses. Scenario 2 would bring in a total of $94,300 in revenue and $211,668 in expenses, while scenario 3 would bring in a total of $122,320 in revenue and $274,047 in expenses. The study also found much of the staffing is provided by volunteers, including volunteers from South Shore Senior Partners equating to half an FTE of staffing efforts. With South Shore Senior Partners planning to disband by the end of December 2026, the city council considered options for future staffing. "I think the loss of the Senior Partners is a huge loss, they really supported that senior programming. When you look at other cities, senior programming doesn't make money but it is a huge community asset and very important and vital for those members," Czech added. "We have some dedicated volunteers and I think we just want to make their volunteer experience an enjoyable one where they can come in, they're excited, they're passionate and they can do the things that they want to do." Therefore, the city plans to discuss further the task force's recommendations to define and communicate a clear facility identity, implement intentional scheduling, align pricing with market position and demand, develop a customer-focused marketing program, enhance the customer experience, align staffing and operations with operational goals, and implement strategic facility improvements.
